symptom: ako/mxcli#1934 (mendixlabs/mxcli#1732): `marketplace update 170 --to 11.5.1 --force` (Community Commons) failed with "install the new version's bundled files: open package target.mpk: … no such file or directory" after it had already dropped the installed module and copied units: the project was left half-updated (245 files deleted in mprcontents/) and had to be restored from git.
cause: Two defects. The caller derived the package path itself as work/target.mpk, while referenceFor(…, "t") downloads to work/t.mpk — so every update looked for a file that never existed. And PerformUpdate read the package only after `drop module`, TransplantModule, identity and grant restore, so the missing input surfaced after the destructive steps.
file: cmd/mxcli/cmd_marketplace_diff.go (referenceFor returns the package path it downloaded to), cmd/mxcli/cmd_marketplace_update.go (uses it; no 'mid-update' warning when nothing was written), cmd/mxcli/marketplace/update.go (preflightUpdate before the drop: reference project opens and holds the module, package opens; ErrUpdateNotStarted)
insight: A destructive multi-step operation must read every input it will need before the first write — the order, not just the input, was the bug: with the path fixed, a corrupt download or a reference without the module would still have stranded the project. And a path two functions agree on by convention ('the slot letter plus .mpk') belongs to one of them: returning it from referenceFor makes the mismatch impossible rather than corrected. The test hashes every file of a fixture project before and after PerformUpdate with a missing package / reference project; on main both cases changed the project (the reported 'open package' error after the drop), with the preflight stubbed they fail again. The full command needs the marketplace (a PAT) and mx, so it was not driven end to end here.
